picks.name: You Can See Everything
picks.why: From your wanted list: now out in proper quality (Porrada 2026 WEB-DL 1080p x264 DUAL 5.1).

picks.name: Match Point
picks.why: An ambitious tennis instructor marries into London money, and he is ready to do something monstrous to keep it. Woody Allen's darkest film plays it straight, and its ending is morally sickening.

picks.name: I Saw the Devil
picks.why: A secret agent hunts the serial killer who murdered his fiancée, then lets him go so he can catch him again and make him suffer. Kim Jee-woon's revenge thriller keeps escalating and asks what the hunt turns the hunter into.

picks.name: Headhunters
picks.why: A smug corporate recruiter who steals art on the side robs the wrong man, and the job becomes a hunt for his life. A tight, nasty Norwegian thriller that keeps getting worse for him, with a payoff that clicks into place.

picks.name: Blue Ruin
picks.why: A drifter carries out a clumsy act of revenge and then has to deal with the family that comes after him. It's quiet and grim, and the violence is awkward and frightening, with every step making things worse.

picks.name: Green Room
picks.why: A punk band sees a murder at a neo-Nazi bar and is trapped in the green room while the owners plan how to get rid of them. Jeremy Saulnier's siege thriller is relentless, with sudden violence and real stakes.

picks.name: Nocturnal Animals
picks.why: An art dealer reads her ex-husband's brutal novel, and the story bleeds into her own guilt. Tom Ford controls every frame, the menace keeps rising and the revenge ending is cold.

picks.name: Elle
picks.why: Verhoeven's thriller about a game-company boss who responds to an assault in ways no one expects. Darkly funny, deeply uncomfortable and completely controlled.

picks.name: A Simple Plan
picks.why: Three ordinary men find a crashed plane full of cash, and keeping it turns decent people into killers one reasonable step at a time. Sam Raimi's most precise film.

picks.name: Zodiac
picks.why: Fincher's obsessive serial-killer procedural, where the search eats the lives of the men running it. The basement scene is one of the most frightening sequences of its decade.

new.name: The Whisper Man
new.why: A grieving father and his son move to a town still haunted by a serial killer who may have had an accomplice. A dark crime thriller built on a slowly closing trap.

new.name: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother
new.why: A devout hitman races across Houston to protect his children after his wife dies. A tense crime drama about a violent man whose beliefs are coming apart.

new.name: Other Mommy
new.why: A girl in a home torn by her parents' marriage meets a sinister presence from her closet that calls itself Other Mommy. Domestic horror where the family drama feeds the threat.

new.name: La Grazia
new.why: Sorrentino's drama about a widowed Italian president deciding on euthanasia and pardons for killers while brooding over his late wife's infidelity. Dry and morally knotty.

new.name: Father Mother Sister Brother
new.why: Jarmusch's deadpan triptych of estranged adult children visiting their cool, distant parents. Quiet, dry and painfully awkward.

new.name: V/H/S/Mixtape
new.why: The latest found-footage anthology, built this time around music and sound. A string of short, nasty scares.

new.name: The Death of Robin Hood
new.why: A bleak reinvention with an aging Robin Hood haunted by a life of murder and offered a strange chance at salvation. Grim and violent.

new.name: Zeta
new.why: A Spanish spy hunts a former agent from an old undercover mission while a Colombian operative chases the same man. A cold-blooded espionage thriller about buried secrets.

new.name: Disclosure Day
new.why: Spielberg's sci-fi mystery about what happens when proof arrives that we aren't alone. Builds on paranoia rather than spectacle.

new.name: Nuremberg
new.why: Before the Nuremberg trials, an army psychiatrist examines Hermann Göring and gets pulled into an uneasy bond with him while trying to understand evil. A tense two-hander about a monster who is charming, calm and very persuasive.

dread.name: Lady Macbeth
dread.why: A young woman sold into a loveless marriage in rural 19th-century England starts an affair and then kills to protect it. It's cold, spare and quietly vicious, and it ends on a chilling note.

dread.name: Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance
dread.why: Park Chan-wook's first vengeance film: a kidnapping meant to be harmless spirals into a chain of retribution. Cold, logical and devastating.

dread.name: The Skin I Live In
dread.why: Almodóvar's clinical thriller about a surgeon and the woman held captive in his house. The mid-film reveal recasts everything, and the ending pays it off.

dread.name: A Tale of Two Sisters
dread.why: Two sisters come home to a stepmother and a house that's wrong. A beautifully controlled Korean horror with a twist that cuts deep.

dread.name: Oldboy
dread.why: A man imprisoned for 15 years without explanation is released and given five days to find out why. The revenge plot builds to one of cinema's cruelest reveals.

dread.name: The Invisible Man
dread.why: A woman escapes her controlling partner, then becomes convinced he's still with her. Gaslighting turned into precise, escalating horror.

dread.name: The Witch
dread.why: A banished Puritan family on the edge of a forest turns on itself as something picks off its members. Slow, exact, and dread that never lets up.

dread.name: Possessor
dread.why: A corporate assassin who works by taking over other people's bodies loses her grip on herself. Brandon Cronenberg's cold, savage sci-fi horror.

dread.name: Insomnia
dread.why: A sleepless detective covers up his own mistake while a calm killer blackmails him. A tight moral squeeze under a sun that never sets.

dread.name: Blood Simple
dread.why: The Coens' debut: a jealous bar owner hires a sleazy detective to kill his wife, and every double-cross makes it worse.

deadpan.name: Wild Tales
deadpan.why: An Argentine anthology of six stories in which ordinary people pushed by small slights escalate to wrecked cars, poison and a wedding that turns into a massacre. It is pitch-black and very funny, and every story ends on a sharp punchline.

deadpan.name: The Square
deadpan.why: A polished museum curator's life comes apart after a stolen phone and a viral marketing stunt that goes too far. Ruben Östlund's satire stays bone-dry while respectable people calmly watch things get ugly.

deadpan.name: Triangle of Sadness
deadpan.why: Östlund's satire of models and the ultra-rich on a luxury cruise that goes very wrong. Cool, merciless and played completely straight.

deadpan.name: The King of Comedy
deadpan.why: A delusional would-be comic kidnaps a talk-show host to get his shot. Scorsese plays the horror as calm, sad comedy.

deadpan.name: The Death of Stalin
deadpan.why: Stalin's inner circle scrambles for power over his corpse while the purges go on. Very funny and genuinely monstrous.

deadpan.name: Ingrid Goes West
deadpan.why: An unstable woman moves to LA to insert herself into an influencer's life. Pitch-dark social media satire that never winks.

deadpan.name: Dream Scenario
deadpan.why: A dull professor starts appearing in millions of strangers' dreams, and fame curdles into a mob. Nicolas Cage plays it bone-dry.

deadpan.name: Welcome to the Dollhouse
deadpan.why: Solondz's portrait of a bullied seventh-grader in a cruel suburban family. Deadpan and uncomfortable, and the humiliations are presented with a straight face.

deadpan.name: Young Adult
deadpan.why: A ghostwriter of teen novels returns to her hometown to steal back her married high-school boyfriend. A calmly awful protagonist and a refusal to redeem her.

deadpan.name: I Care a Lot
deadpan.why: A legal guardian strips elderly wards of their assets, then picks the wrong victim. A smiling villain running a monstrous scam as routine business.

deepcuts.name: La cérémonie
deepcuts.why: Chabrol's class thriller about an illiterate maid and a postal clerk who resent a wealthy family. Restrained all the way to a shocking ending.

deepcuts.name: The Clovehitch Killer
deepcuts.why: A Boy Scout in a Christian town begins to suspect his father is a local serial killer. Quiet, suburban and steadily chilling.

deepcuts.name: The Guilty
deepcuts.why: A Danish emergency dispatcher takes a call from a kidnapped woman and tries to save her without leaving his desk. Ninety minutes of rising tension with a crushing turn.

deepcuts.name: Revanche
deepcuts.why: An Austrian ex-con's robbery goes wrong, and he finds himself close to the cop he blames. A slow, tight moral thriller.

deepcuts.name: The Celebration
deepcuts.why: At a patriarch's 60th birthday dinner, his son stands to make a toast that reveals the family's secret. Raw, darkly funny and devastating.

deepcuts.name: Dead Man's Shoes
deepcuts.why: A soldier comes home to take methodical revenge on the small-town thugs who tormented his brother. Brutal, and the reveal changes everything.

deepcuts.name: Red Road
deepcuts.why: A Glasgow CCTV operator spots a man from her past on her screens and begins following him. A quiet surveillance thriller with a sharp ending.

deepcuts.name: Tyrannosaur
deepcuts.why: A violent widower and a charity-shop worker with a secret at home. Harsh British realism in which the cruelty leads to a reckoning.

deepcuts.name: Bedevilled
deepcuts.why: A Seoul banker visits the remote island where her childhood friend is treated like a slave by the whole village. It builds slowly to an explosion of revenge.

deepcuts.name: A Hard Day
deepcuts.why: A corrupt detective hides a body after a hit-and-run, then someone who knows starts calling. A tense, blackly funny Korean thriller.

doubles.name: The Double
doubles.why: A timid office clerk watches his exact double, who is confident and ruthless, take over his job, his crush and his life. Richard Ayoade's dark doppelgänger comedy is dry, airless and steadily menacing.

doubles.name: House of Games
doubles.why: A psychiatrist lets a con man pull her into his world of grifts, and each trick turns out to be part of a bigger one. David Mamet's cold, precise film about performance as a weapon, with an ending that bites.

doubles.name: Nightmare Alley
doubles.why: A drifter learns the carnival mentalist act and takes it into high society, posing as a real psychic until the role destroys him. Del Toro's noir is a slow tightening toward a brutal, perfectly set-up ending.

doubles.name: Body Double
doubles.why: An out-of-work actor is drawn into voyeurism and witnesses a murder that may have been staged for him. Brian De Palma's twisty thriller about performers, setups and roles played for real.

doubles.name: Vertigo
doubles.why: A detective obsessed with a dead woman remakes a lookalike in her image, not knowing who is really playing whom. Hitchcock's darkest study of doubles, impersonation and obsession.

doubles.name: Persona
doubles.why: A nurse caring for an actress who has stopped speaking finds their identities starting to merge. Bergman's short, unsettling and controlled film is the template for every story about one self taking over another.

doubles.name: Holy Motors
doubles.why: A man rides through Paris in a limousine all day, taking on 'appointments' as a killer, a beggar, a father and a monster, with no audience in sight. Leos Carax's strange tribute to acting as something lived for real.

doubles.name: Sisters
doubles.why: A reporter sees a murder through a window, and the trail leads to a model and her separated conjoined twin. De Palma's early thriller is lurid on the surface but built with real control and a nasty sting.

doubles.name: Orphan
doubles.why: A grieving couple adopts a poised, unsettling girl who is not what she seems at all. A well-made impostor horror film whose twist reframes everything before it.

doubles.name: The Stepfather
doubles.why: A perfect suburban dad is really a killer who keeps wiping out families and starting over under a new name. Terry O'Quinn's calm, smiling performance as a man playing 'father' as a role makes this a sharp B-thriller.

series.name: Pluribus
series.why: Vince Gilligan's tightly controlled sci-fi series about one bitter woman who stays immune when the rest of humanity is calmly absorbed into forced happiness. The menace builds every episode, and the dark humor is bone-dry.

series.name: The Night Of
series.why: A college student wakes beside a murdered woman and is swallowed by the justice system. Tight and grim, and every episode tightens the vise.

series.name: Ripley
series.why: Steven Zaillian's black-and-white Highsmith adaptation of a con man who murders his way into a rich man's life. Cold, precise and patient.

series.name: Mare of Easttown
series.why: A worn-out small-town detective investigates a teenage mother's murder while her own life falls apart. Each episode lands a turn, and the ending is excellent.

series.name: Happy Valley
series.why: A Yorkshire police sergeant crosses paths again with the man who destroyed her family. Brutal, smart and very hard to stop watching.

series.name: The Sinner
series.why: A young mother stabs a stranger to death on a beach and has no idea why. Each season peels back a buried trauma.

series.name: Big Little Lies
series.why: A murder at a school fundraiser in wealthy Monterey, told through the mothers lying to each other. Glossy, cruel and well paced.

series.name: True Detective
series.why: Two Louisiana detectives chase a ritualistic killer across 17 years. The first season is a slow-burn crime story with real dread.
